title: Google login
summary: Configure Google OpenID Connect login using Spring Security’s managed flow.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: OAuth2 in Spring Boot | How to Add Google Login in Spring Boot | Complete Tutorial

richText: Use spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client in a Spring Boot 3 application.
Register the application as an OAuth client with Google. Google supplies a client ID and client secret.
Register the exact callback URL that Google will use to return to the application.
Keep the client secret on the server. Supply it through environment configuration or a secret manager.

example.title: Configure Google and enable browser login
description: Use a Spring Boot 3 servlet web application with the OAuth2 client starter.
Set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET in the application environment.
For local development on port 8080, register http://localhost:8080/login/oauth2/code/google with Google.
Put the properties in application.properties and the bean in a @Configuration class.
Import Bean, Customizer, HttpSecurity and SecurityFilterChain.
explanation: The google registration name selects Spring’s built-in Google provider defaults.
openid requests OIDC login. profile and email request profile information.
Spring handles the callback, exchanges the code and validates the OIDC response.
After login, the application remembers authentication with a server session.
CSRF remains enabled because the browser sends the session cookie automatically.
For deployment, register the public HTTPS callback URL. A reverse proxy must preserve the correct public host and protocol.

richText: Associate the external identity with an account
Identify an external account by its verified issuer and subject (sub).
Email addresses can change. Do not use email alone as a permanent external account key.
Assign local roles through the application’s account rules. Google login does not automatically give an ADMIN role.
Keep account-linking rules explicit before joining an external identity to an existing account.
